importance_ranking.reason: Polyhouse type (NVPH vs Fan & Pad vs shade net) and structure material are non-interchangeable — wrong type means wrong subsidy category and wrong crop suitability. Specs are the primary shortlisting gate before any other signal is evaluated.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Established EPC firms (Dhaanya Seeds, Hitech Polyhouses, Jain Irrigation polyhouse division) carry buyer recall; buyers also actively search for state-empanelled contractors by name for subsidy-linked projects.
importance_ranking.reason: Subsidy-linked projects require contractors empanelled with state horticulture departments who can prepare DPRs and pass JIT inspections — contractor identity is a regulatory-equivalent trust gate, not a preference.

Project cost varies substantially by polyhouse type, area, and structure grade; Indian buyers are price-sensitive but can only compare prices after type and scope are confirmed. Listed price is a budget entry point; final cost is always negotiated per project scope.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per sq ft dominates B2B buyer-facing negotiation; per sq meter is used in NHB/MIDH DPR and subsidy documentation; large projects (1 acre+) are often quoted as lump-sum turnkey. Unit must be shown alongside price to prevent misreading across these conventions.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per sq meter vs per project (lump sum) creates genuine price comparison confusion — a buyer comparing two listings cannot interpret price without knowing the unit basis.

Portfolio photos of completed polyhouse projects serve as build-quality and contractor-credibility evidence, but the product is a construction service — type, specs, and contractor credentials carry more decision weight than visual appearance.
